expectations.text: Output warns that total registered users (25,000) cannot be used as eligible traffic for this experiment
expectations.evidence: Output identifies 3,750/month as eligible users but does not warn that 25,000 cannot be used. Instead, it presents 'Scenario 2: Using All Users (Including Existing)' suggesting total users could be included.

expectations.text: Output correctly identifies that only new sign-ups are eligible (approximately 15% of 25,000 = ~3,750/month)
expectations.evidence: Line 13-14: 'New Sign-ups Rate: 15% per month' and 'Eligible Users per Month: 3,750 users/month (25,000 × 0.15)'

expectations.text: Output provides a sample size per group in the range 1,200–2,000 users
expectations.evidence: Lines 47, 53, 109: 'n ≈ 3,077 users per arm' - significantly exceeds the expected range of 1,200–2,000

expectations.text: Output does NOT calculate duration using 25,000 as eligible traffic (would give an incorrectly short duration of ~0.12 weeks or ~1 day)
expectations.evidence: Line 65: Duration calculated as '1.6 months' using 3,750/month, not 25,000. No calculation using 25,000 as eligible traffic is present.

expectations.text: Output either blocks the duration estimate pending confirmation of eligible traffic, or calculates it using the ~3,750/month figure
expectations.evidence: Line 65: 'Time required: 1.6 months (~6 weeks)' calculated using 3,750 new sign-ups/month for Scenario 1

claims: The sample size calculation appears inflated (3,077 per arm vs expected ~1,500-1,600)
The output does not explicitly warn against using 25,000 as eligible traffic; instead it presents a secondary scenario using all users

suggestions: Review sample size calculation methodology - result is roughly 2x higher than expected (~3,077 vs ~1,500-1,600)
Add explicit warning that 25,000 total users cannot be used as eligible traffic; restrict to new sign-ups only
Remove or clarify 'Scenario 2: Using All Users' as it conflates different eligible populations
eval_feedback.overall: Output provides structured analysis but fails key assertions: sample size is too large (3,077 vs 1,200-2,000 expected range), and does not warn against using total platform users (25,000) as eligible traffic. The output also presents a competing scenario that suggests total users could be included, which undermines assertion 1.
